Durable Objects SQLite is the default storage now

In 2025 Cloudflare made SQLite-backed Durable Objects the recommended storage path. KV is still fine for write-rarely configuration, but coordinated clip jobs should keep their cursor in a Durable Object rather than hoping R2 listings are strongly consistent.

Why this matters for a read-later pipeline

A Queue consumer can retry. If translate already succeeded, re-running the whole pipeline burns gpt-4.1-mini tokens. The job record in R2 is the source of truth for OPDS, but the in-flight cursor belongs in SQLite so two retries do not clip the same URL twice.

  1. Accept POST /clip and enqueue { jobId, runId, url }.
  2. Persist the run in Durable Object SQLite before the first fetch.
  3. Write EPUB to R2 only after translate returns Japanese Markdown.

Workers AI is not a drop-in translator

Workers AI can host small models next to the Worker, which looks tempting next to GPT-5.6 Terra pricing. For English-to-Japanese long-form with fenced code, a dedicated chat completion still wins. Keep code fences untouched: 

export class ClipCursor {
  constructor(state: DurableObjectState) {
    this.sql = state.storage.sql
  }
}

Do not summarize the article. The Xteink user is reading later, not skimming a chatbot digest.

See the Durable Objects storage guide. Names such as Hyperdrive, Vectorize, and Workflows stay in English on first use, with a short Japanese gloss only if the sentence would otherwise be opaque.
